note: The environment probe is the interesting half: it reports what it cannot do rather than failing, which is what makes it usable on a hardened host.
verdict_reason: A 33 KB file manager written as a small number of very long lines at wp-includes/Text/Diff/lang/index.php - a real core directory that upstream ships no index.php in. verdict_reason: An uploader at wp-content/uploads/wpcode/d/g/index.php: prints php_uname() and exec('pwd'), then copies an uploaded file into $_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT'], falling back to the current directory when the root is not writable, and prints the resulting URL. note: Classified benign on the same principle as failed-fetch-404-artefact: attacker-written is not the same as malicious, and the verdict is about what the file does. That one is inert HTML and flagging it would be plainly wrong; this one is PHP that disables error reporting and touches $_FILES in wp-admin/network/, and a rule that flags it is defensible. Pinning it would constrain a future rule for no benefit.
